questions.question: Why is the variable sliding window still O(n) even though it has a while loop inside a for loop?
options: Because the inner loop runs at most once per outer iteration
Because left and right each only move forward, so together they make at most about 2n moves
Because JavaScript optimises nested loops automatically
It is not O(n); it is O(n²) in the worst case
questions.explanation: Each element enters the window once (right moves) and leaves at most once (left moves), so the total work across all iterations is linear.

questions.question: The 'shortest subarray with sum at least target' window template gives a wrong answer for [1, -5, 4, 3] with target 7. Why?
options: The window size must be fixed
The answer must be recorded after the while loop
Shrinking assumes adding an element always increases the sum, which negative numbers break
questions.explanation: With negatives, the running sum is not monotonic, so the window logic can miss valid ranges. Prefix sums with a hash map handle negatives.

questions.question: In the longest-substring-without-repeating-characters solution, why check lastSeen.get(ch) >= left before moving left?
options: So that a character last seen before the current window does not move left backwards
To keep the Map size under 26
To make the algorithm work on sorted strings
questions.explanation: An old occurrence outside the window is irrelevant; without the check, left could jump backwards and the window would include duplicates.

questions.question: What is the time complexity of finding the maximum sum of every k consecutive elements with a fixed sliding window?
questions.explanation: After computing the first window, each slide adds one element and subtracts one, so the whole pass is O(n) regardless of k.
